question: Does the old shared phase-response matrix predict fresh-source responses, and is nearby-frequency variation more consistent with a fixed coefficient map or a fixed output delay?

design.question: Does the old shared phase-response matrix predict fresh-source responses, and is nearby-frequency variation more consistent with a fixed coefficient map or a fixed output delay?
design.recommended_stage: First validate frozen shared H on16 fresh backgrounds at the same2 centers. Optional nearby-frequency control is separately declared and not required for the first-stage decision.
design.source_design: 16 fresh independent seeds,4 per the same balanced/far,dominant/far,balanced/near,dominant/near mixture types; context128 and horizon32; all4 common phases crossed independently of background phases.
design.immutable_predictor: Use all16 old source matrices to form one frozen arithmetic-mean H per model/policy/frequency, saved in frozen_H.json now. Do not refit any predictive H on the fresh sources. Fresh per-source H may be estimated only as an explicitly optimistic diagnostic ceiling.
design.primary_contrasts: Phase-energy-pooled waveform NMSE: identity versus old frozen H on each fresh source;16 paired source differences, source win counts, source-stratified4096 bootstrap draws; retain all backgrounds and type summaries. Native and locked separate. No confirmatory p-values.
design.secondary: Complex-linear and symmetric-traceless decomposition, singular values, DC-adjusted sensitivity, exact off-band/even closure; compare predicted systematic structure with fresh conditional variation.

optional_nearby_control.candidate1: Hold H fixed at its nearest trained center.
optional_nearby_control.candidate2: Freeze principal tau=-arg(q+i*r)/omega_center from old mean H. At nearby omega use H_delay(omega)=R(-(omega-omega_center)*tau) @ H_center, rotating the entire output map; it matches H_center exactly at the trained frequency.
optional_nearby_control.interpretation: Tests a frequency-phase law, not an identified patch mechanism. Principal tau is modulo-period ambiguous. Large off-band response can make projected phase misleading; report DC and off-band controls.

design.anchoring_followup_proposal: Before extra native variants, separately preregister a reuse-only fit on forecast windows0:16,16:32 and0:32 using their original absolute future timestamps, plus DC-adjusted fits. Horizon-varying apparent lag argues against a single pure delay but does not identify patch causality. An information-preserving masked-prefix padding test would require its own validated parity gates; ordinary history shifts change context and are confounded.
design.gates: Exact repeat/normalizer self identity; source/checkpoint/bank hashes; nominal and antipodal input checks; no failed or outcome-replaced source. Persist raw forecasts and knowledge after every execution.
design.execution_state: No input bank generated, no capture driver launched, no native slot requested or occupied. Coordinator slot grant and a frozen capture protocol/addendum are required before any execution.
design.broad_grid: Closed; original full grid remains unlaunched.

controls: Exact repeat/normalizer self identity; source/checkpoint/bank hashes; nominal and antipodal input checks; no failed or outcome-replaced source. Persist raw forecasts and knowledge after every execution.
limitations: Only a proposal. Repeated phases are not independent sources. Fixed-delay transport is a conditional diagnostic, not proof of time invariance or patch anchoring.
evidence_class: Prospective design with frozen old-data predictors; no fresh-model evidence
next_decision: Coordinator reviews same-center first-stage proposal and optional discriminator. No native slot granted or used.
